p: The NEC side of Birmingham works very differently from the city centre, and that's worth knowing before you book. On big show days and concert nights, the roads and car parks around Marston Green get seriously busy, so leave more time than you think to get in and parked. If your group can come by train, Birmingham International station is linked to the airport and the NEC, and from there it's a walk across to Resorts World.

Timing your game well makes all the difference. Book a slot that leaves breathing space before doors open at any event, because nobody wants to be racing the escape room clock and the gig clock on the same afternoon. An early game followed by food is often the most relaxed way to do it.

Escape rooms suit all sorts of groups, but it's worth agreeing a few ground rules before you go in. Decide who's keeping an eye on the timer, who's collecting found items, and who'll ask for a hint if everyone's stuck. It saves arguments later.

Resorts World sits beside Pendigo Lake, which is pleasant for a quick wander once you've escaped, and the wider NEC site hosts everything from huge exhibitions to big-name concerts. Motorbike fans can also find the National Motorcycle Museum nearby at Bickenhill, just off the M42, which makes a decent add-on for a full day on this side of the city. Note that parts of the Resorts World complex are for over-18s only, so keep that in mind if you're bringing teenagers along.
